briefed_task: Settle whether #2786's GB10 decode shortfall (ratio_median 0.579x) is warm-up or a real deficit. Two discriminators: (1) plot the trial ordering, (2) does a longer warmup move the median.
verdict: REAL DEFICIT. Not warm-up, not clock settling, not thermal.
headline: apr's steady-state decode on GB10 is 106.4 tok/s [95% CI 103.1-110.0] against ollama's 182.9 on the same box = 0.582x, measured by a 24-point token ladder that does not use the gate's differencing estimator at all. That is, to three digits, what the gate already reported. The ratio_best/ratio_median gap that motivated the warm-up hypothesis is a property of the estimator (256000/Delta is a reciprocal, hence right-skewed) and is reproduced exactly by simulating a CONSTANT 106.4 tok/s.

protocol_honesty: NOT APR-PERF-GATE-001 §4.4.2. §4.4.2 (2 x c warmup + 5 s quiesce) governs the perf-matrix BAND harness and §4.4.3 defines decode_tok_s INSIDE a request. beat_ollama_decode_throughput_speed.rs is a different harness with NO warmup step at all, deriving a rate by differencing two independent cold one-shot process invocations. There was no §4.4.2 knob to enlarge, so discriminator 2 was implemented directly (a full discard invocation before each measured pair) and backed by a token ladder that removes the differencing entirely.

discriminator_1_trial_ordering.verdict: NO TREND - warm-up weakened before any GPU time was spent
discriminator_1_trial_ordering.note: The two runs put the maximum in different places (trial 7 vs trial 3). No ramp.

discriminator_2_longer_warmup.design: 7 trials per arm, arms INTERLEAVED (cold, warm, cold, warm...) against host drift. cold = exactly the gate's protocol. warm = a full 384-token discard invocation immediately before the measured pair.
discriminator_2_longer_warmup.floor_gap: the floor needs +55%; a 6.4% non-significant shift is not the explanation
discriminator_2_longer_warmup.key_corroboration: The COLD arm reproduces CI run 33292383055 EXACTLY at 0.579x. The gate is repeatable.

discriminator_3_added_token_ladder.verdict: STEADY-STATE RATE IS 106.4 tok/s AND IS FLAT WITH DEPTH
discriminator_3_added_token_ladder.design: apr run --gpu --benchmark --max-tokens N for N in {128,256,384,512,768,1024}, 4 reps, fit t(N) = C + N/R. Removes the gate's differencing entirely.
discriminator_3_added_token_ladder.quadratic_check: marginal 109.4 tok/s at N=256 -> 102.6 at N=1024; residual sd 233 -> 236 ms, so the linear model stands. No regime the gate's 128->384 window is missing.
discriminator_3_added_token_ladder.three_estimators_agree: ladder OLS 0.582x, ladder Theil-Sen 0.586x, cold gate arm 0.579x, against the CI's 0.579x / 0.647x

discriminator_4_added_estimator_skew.verdict: ratio_best > ratio_median NEEDS NO WARM REGIME - it is a property of the estimator
discriminator_4_added_estimator_skew.mechanism: rate = 256000 / Delta is the RECIPROCAL of a noisy difference, so its sampling distribution is right-skewed: when Delta lands low the reported rate blows up. best sits far above median even at a perfectly constant rate.
discriminator_4_added_estimator_skew.simulation: constant R = 106.4 tok/s (the ladder fit), per-invocation jitter 233 ms each side => 330 ms on the difference, median-of-7 and best-of-7, 200000 draws
discriminator_4_added_estimator_skew.conclusion: All six observed values fall inside the constant-rate prediction. Nothing is left for warm-up, scheduling or clock settling to explain.

discriminator_5_added_gpu_clocking.verdict: THE GPU IS NOT CLOCKING DOWN

clock_trace_100ms_of_one_cold_apr_run_10.phase_1_0_to_3.45s: P8, 208 MHz, 4.4 W, util 0 - host-side load, GPU asleep
clock_trace_100ms_of_one_cold_apr_run_10.phase_2_3.45_to_9.58s: P0, 2411 MHz, ~11 W, util 0 - CUDA context up, GPU IDLE
clock_trace_100ms_of_one_cold_apr_run_10.phase_3_9.58_to_12.46s: P0, 2411 MHz, 15->60 W, util 0 - weight cache / graph capture

discriminator_5_added_gpu_clocking.no_ramp: P8 -> P0 is a SINGLE 120 ms sample: 208 MHz -> 2411 MHz. There is no gradual ramp to settle into. Ceiling is 3003 MHz; decode ran 2411-2522 MHz at 43-56 degC.

matched_clock_probe.reading: same clock, comparable power, ~1.7x the throughput for ollama

discriminator_5_added_gpu_clocking.lifetime_throttle_counters_after_1h_of_b: HW Thermal Slowdown 0 us | SW Thermal Slowdown 0 us | HW Power Braking 0 us
discriminator_5_added_gpu_clocking.sw_power_cap_note: 'SW Power Cap: Active' reads at IDLE on this part at 4.5 W and goes Not Active under load - an idle-state artifact, not a workload throttle.

what_the_harness_does_get_wrong.verdict: NOISE, NOT BIAS - the gate is noisy, not wrong
what_the_harness_does_get_wrong.mechanism: The differential's signal is Delta ~ 2.4 s sitting on a fixed cost of C ~ 8.6 s in apr's own timer (~12.5 s of process wall before the first decoded token = 61% of a 20 s invocation). Per-invocation jitter of 233 ms becomes 14% CV in the reported rate.
what_the_harness_does_get_wrong.evidence: apr CV 12.7-15.0% vs ollama CV 0.41-0.75%, same box, minutes apart. apr's median moved 11.6% between the two CI runs; ollama's moved 0.04%.
what_the_harness_does_get_wrong.unbiasedness: cold gate median 106.0 vs ladder fit 106.4 - the noise is symmetric and the median is unbiased.
what_the_harness_does_get_wrong.practical_consequence: a single night's ratio_median carries a simulated 95% band of 0.520-0.665 around the truth, so the gate should not be read to two decimal places.
what_the_harness_does_get_wrong.I9_consequence: These gx10 runs were NOT spent through an inadequate warmup. The measurement is sound and the cells it informs are not burned.

side_finding_A_yield_guard_blind_on_gb10.verdict: CONFIRMED, did NOT cause the shortfall, but is a real hole
side_finding_A_yield_guard_blind_on_gb10.what: Both failing runs logged 'GPU memory.used=0 MiB, existing compute procs=0' while PID 32612 -- ./target/release/apr serve run ...q4_k_m.gguf --gpu-layers all --port 8451 -- had been resident since 2026-08-27 17:45 (66 h at measurement time).
side_finding_A_yield_guard_blind_on_gb10.why: nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps returns nothing on GB10's unified memory, and memory.used reads [N/A]. cuda-nightly.yml calls procs 'the primary, portable signal - it works on both sm_89 and GB10'. On this silicon it does not.
side_finding_A_yield_guard_blind_on_gb10.not_the_cause: that serve process is idle - GPU measured 0% / 208 MHz / 4.5 W with it resident
side_finding_A_yield_guard_blind_on_gb10.consequence: the guard cannot see a busy GB10 and so cannot yield to training on it

side_finding_B_ollama_arm_can_run_away.verdict: CONFIRMED, a live flake source in the comparator arm
side_finding_B_ollama_arm_can_run_away.what: `ollama run <model> <prompt> --verbose` is unbounded; ollama context-shifts and keeps generating. One of five trials here ran 283 s before being killed by PID; its neighbours produced 758-1280 tokens in 4-7 s.
side_finding_B_ollama_arm_can_run_away.corroboration: run 33292383055's ollama trials=[154.99, 182.79, 182.9, 182.35, 100.85] - a first-trial warm-up plus a 45% collapse on trial 5 - is consistent with this. Median-of-5 absorbed it that night.

scope.says: on GB10, apr decodes this model at ~106 tok/s against ollama's ~183, at the same SM clock, on the same weights, with no throttling and no warm-up effect. The >=0.90x no-collapse floor is genuinely violated by a genuine ~1.7x kernel/pipeline gap.
scope.does_not_say: nothing about Ada; not that GB10 is a slow machine (the gate is a RATIO on one box, and ollama reaches 183 tok/s on that same box); does not identify the responsible kernel.
scope.next_question: which kernel - this is now a kernel question rather than a measurement question
scope.spec_note: APR-PERF-GATE-001 §4.3.1's 'GB10 legitimately loses ~4x on decode while winning prefill' concerns ABSOLUTE decode against other silicon; it does not excuse a ratio measured against a comparator on the same GB10.
